models/SpotModel.h.note: Panadapter spot store (callsign/freq/mode/lifetime/priority) on canonical state; kv ingest is trivially generic

models/TnfModel.h.note: Tracking notch filter state (freq/width/depth/permanent, global enable) — generic DSP notch surface; kv parse is transport detail

models/TransmitModel.h.note: TX state model: power/MOX/VOX/CW/filter are core-profile; ATU, DAX, APD, profiles, interlock are Flex.
models/TransmitModel.h.split: Core: RF/tune power, MOX/PTT+Quindar, VOX, mic level/proc, CW params, TX filter, monitor. Flex: ATU, DAX, APD samplers, TX/mic profiles, interlock ACC/RCA delays+polarity, SmartSDR status-kv parsing/commands.

models/TunerModel.h.note: External-tuner state model, intended to become vendor-neutral (usable by any 3rd-party tuner). Fuses universal tuner state with Flex-specific TGXL wiring, so it's mixed — NOT peripheral (that's the transport TgxlConnection) and NOT pure vendor. Distinct from the radio's own built-in ATU (TransmitModel).
models/TunerModel.h.split: Core (universal, stays the model the UI/3rd-party sees): operate/bypass/tuning state, SWR/fwd-power, antenna-switch selection, presence. Flex extension (move behind FlexBackend as an IRadioBackend extension verb): the TGXL radio-relay — SmartSDR atu/tgxl/amplifier passthrough (commandReady, atu-status decode), which is the ONLY control path for remote/SmartLink operation and is TGXL-specific (the radio relays only the TGXL). A direct TgxlConnection (peripheral, port 9010) is the local fast-path. 2.3-style split; see #4092.

models/XvtrPolicy.h.note: XVTR policy: transverter list/freq translation is core; waterfall-tile offset + FLEX model power clamps are flex
models/XvtrPolicy.h.split: Core: Transverter struct, RF/IF frequency mapping intent. Flex: ModelCapabilities-based band-stack keys, waterfall tile offset matching, FLEX-64/6600 max-power dBm ranges.

core/AcomProtocol.h.note: ACOM S-series RS-232 amplifier wire protocol (framing, checksums, per-model power scaling) — the codec half of core/AcomConnection.h. A standalone accessory's own transport with no radio-family awareness, same precedent as the Tgxl/Pgxl direct sockets: peripheral, NOT behind the IRadioBackend radio seam. Authority: the manufacturer's published 600S serial-protocol spec.

core/AetherClockEngine.h.note: WWV/WWVB time-signal decode engine bound to an operator-chosen RX slice. Deliberately source-agnostic: the wiring layer injects a DAX-hold provider and any 24 kHz float32-stereo feed drives it, so the engine never touches a vendor stream class (its own header documents this as EB3 discipline). Canonical engine state.

core/AetherClockSettings.h.note: AetherClock persistence — one nested JSON blob under a single AppSettings key (Principle V). Client-side config plumbing; radio-authoritative state (slice frequency, mode, AGC) is deliberately never persisted here.

core/AetherDspModePolicy.h.note: Pure policy deciding when AetherDSP must disable for a given mode or slice audio mix. Operates on canonical mode/mute/gain state only; no vendor ties.

core/AutomationBridgeSettings.h.note: Owned configuration for the agent automation bridge (enabled / txAllowed / txAck / readOnly) under one nested key; the secret token lives in the OS keychain, not here. Dev and test tooling — same home decision as core/AutomationServer.h. NOTE for RFC §6: txAllowed() is read as a TX-guard input by BOTH AutomationServer and Hl2Backend, so this header is a step-4 consolidation target.

core/ClockAlignmentFrame.h.note: Frozen per-second alignment contract emitted by the AetherClock engine (cross-PR contract, PRD-A §5). Radio-agnostic decode output.

core/ClockDiagnostics.h.note: AetherClock ~1 Hz acquisition-telemetry snapshot (pre-lock funnel, verdict line, debug pane). Measured decode-chain quantities only, parallel to the frozen alignment contract; no vendor ties.

core/DigitalVoiceFeature.h.note: Build-flag and availability filtering for digital-voice modes. Radio-agnostic mode-list logic over the DV registry.

core/DigitalVoiceModeRegistry.h.note: Registry of digital-voice mode descriptors (id, settings id, display name, radio mode, underlying mode, waveform name). Canonical mode metadata; no wire coupling.

core/DigitalVoiceWaveformProcess.h.note: Supervisor for the host-side DV waveform helper process (ThumbDV) — QProcess lifecycle plus a UDP control/data path. The supervision half is universal, but the health surface it publishes counts Flex VITA sequence gaps, so the header is not vendor-neutral as it stands.
core/DigitalVoiceWaveformProcess.h.split: Core (universal): helper-process lifecycle and state machine, endpoint configuration, start/stop/restart policy, turnaround timing. Flex extension: VITA sequence-gap counters (m_vitaSequenceGapsTotal / m_txVitaSequenceGapsTotal) — a DAX/VITA-49 stream fact that a backend should report through the seam rather than the waveform host reading it directly.

core/DigitalVoiceWaveformSettings.h.note: AppSettings-backed DV waveform configuration (backend selection, executable paths). Client-side persistence plumbing, not radio state.

core/HostVoiceChainPolicy.h.note: Decides when the Flex-shaped voice controls (PROC, 8-band graphic EQ) may write the SHARED ClientComp/ClientEq objects the Aetherial strip also edits — two surfaces onto one object, so 'may we write' has a wrong answer (#4609). Universal DSP-ownership question, answered today from Flex-shaped state.
core/HostVoiceChainPolicy.h.split: Core (universal): the chainOwned ownership bit and the write-arbitration predicates over a shared client DSP chain — any backend with two control surfaces onto one processor needs exactly this. Flex extension: the fact that the competing surface's state arrives from a Flex `eq`/`transmit` status (EqualizerModel/TransmitModel have no persistence of their own), which is what forces the bit to be process-local rather than restored.

core/IssueReport.h.note: Renders a pre-filled GitHub issue body from a SupportBundle snapshot, with PII redaction applied at the render boundary (GHSA-ccrg-j8cp-qhc4). Support and diagnostics tooling; not radio state.

core/KiwiSdrTxMutePolicy.h.note: Pure latch (no Kiwi wire types, header-only) encoding KiwiSDR-specific TX-mute semantics: release the mute on this client's optimistic local unkey, but keep gating transmissions this client never keyed (VOX, CAT, hardware PTT, other clients) on the radio-reported interlock. Generic shape, family-specific law.
core/KiwiSdrTxMutePolicy.h.split: Core (universal): the two-source TX-mute latch — local optimistic unkey vs authoritative radio interlock, resolved on the interlock's falling edge. Kiwi extension: that the muted audio source is a separate receive-only stream at all, which stops being a special case once the Kiwi path moves behind IRadioBackend (§5.5) and the mute becomes ordinary per-source TX policy.

core/LocationAddressResolver.h.note: Reverse-geocoding helper backing the GPS location dialog. Network/OS plumbing; no radio state.

core/N1MMSpotClient.h.note: UDP listener for N1MMSpot XML bandmap spots from contest loggers (N1MM+, DXLog), emitting explicit add/delete events (#2906). Radio-agnostic spot ingestion — 'SmartSDR-CAT compatible' names the third-party protocol it mimics, not a dependency on the radio wire.

core/N1MMSpotParser.h.note: Parser and value type for N1MM/DXLog spot documents, including the (dxcall, band) spot key. Radio-agnostic spot data.

core/RadioSettingsScope.h.note: A (family, radioId) handle into the radio-scoped settings store (RFC #4603). Family-neutral by construction — Flex serial, HL2 MAC and Kiwi profile UUID all resolve through the same scope, with radio → family-wide → empty fallback. This is the shape radio-scoped state should keep after the protocol lands.

core/SettingsBootstrap.h.note: Pre-QApplication settings access (RFC #4603) for the two consumers that need a value before the app object exists: the UiScale bootstrap and the RHI backend choice. Client startup plumbing.

core/SettingsCredentialPolicy.h.note: The single source of truth for which settings names are credentials (RFC #4603 proposal E — credentials live only in QtKeychain, never in the settings store). Client security plumbing.

core/SettingsDatabase.h.note: RAII wrapper around the vendored SQLite amalgamation backing the client settings store (RFC #4603); the only TU permitted to include sqlite3.h. Client persistence plumbing.

core/SettingsPaths.h.note: Single source of truth for every path in the client settings store (RFC #4603), replacing three drifted hand-copies of the config-dir logic. Client persistence plumbing.

core/SettingsSanitizer.h.note: Recursive secret-safe rendering of the settings store for the support bundle and `--config export` (RFC #4603). Diagnostics plumbing.

core/TimeFrameVoter.h.note: Shared AetherClock time-frame types plus confidence-weighted cross-frame bit voting over a sliding window. Map-agnostic pure DSP/logic — no Qt, no GUI, no vendor ties.

core/UlanziDialMappings.h.note: Owner of the Ulanzi Dial's pill→action bindings in one feature-owned document (Principle V). A control surface's own configuration — it belongs to the peripheral, not to any radio — same home decision as the FlexControl USB knob.

core/WaterfallRate.h.note: The single definition of what the 1..100 'WtrFall Rate' control means (low is slow, high is fast). A universal display concept that carries TWO conversion laws, deliberately not the same function, because who turns rate into rows differs per family (#3104, #4606).
core/WaterfallRate.h.split: Core (universal): the 1..100 control semantics and the local* law used by any backend that streams raw spectra and has no radio-side display engine (HL2, demo). Flex extension: the flex* law — a steeply non-linear conversion known only by measurement of a Flex display engine, plus the `line_duration` wire-name trap that runs the control backwards if a backend reads FlexLib's milliseconds literally. The flex* half belongs behind FlexBackend once pan geometry converts.

core/WsprBeacon.h.note: WSPR type-1 message encoder and sample-accurate continuous-phase 4-FSK generator (lock-free, allocation-free on the audio thread). Radio-agnostic engine DSP.

core/backends/IRadioBackend.h.note: THE radio seam (RFC §5.5) — the canonical intent verbs, typed deltas and normalized signals every family implements. Universal by definition: the UI reaching this header is the seam working as designed, not coupling. Everything below it in core/backends/<family>/ is family-private.

core/backends/hl2/Hl2Discovery.h.note: HPSDR Protocol 1 ('Metis') discovery for the Hermes-Lite 2, shaped to emit RadioInfo with family="hl2" so the existing picker slots consume it unchanged. Family wire code that belongs below the seam; reached today from ConnectionPanel.cpp, MainWindow.h and RadioSetupDialog.cpp. Pre-existing coupling, frozen into the EB3 baseline — the fix is a family-neutral discovery aggregator behind IRadioBackend, not a wider baseline.

core/backends/hl2/Hl2EmergencyStop.h.note: Async-signal-safe release path for the Hermes-Lite 2 (an HL2 left streaming at a dead host keeps sending EP6, stops answering discovery, and needs a physical power cycle — reproduced three times). Family wire behavior invoked from main.cpp's signal handler; pre-existing coupling, frozen into the EB3 baseline. Generalizes to an engine-level 'release every backend on fatal signal' hook.

core/backends/hl2/MetisProtocol.h.note: HPSDR Protocol 1 ('Metis') wire primitives for the HL2 backend — register map, EP2/EP6 framing, LNA gain register. Family wire code below the seam; reached today from ConnectionPanel.cpp, frozen into the EB3 baseline. Authority: openHPSDR Protocol 1 plus the Hermes-Lite 2 gateware RTL (Principle I, per-backend).

core/backends/sim/NoiseMixer.h.note: Demo-mode synthetic AUDIO engine (RFC #4288 Phase 2b) — additive HF-noise and signal channels feeding SimBackend's audioFrameReady. Backend-internal generator reached from DemoApplet.cpp; family-specific below-seam code, frozen into the EB3 baseline. Demo-mode controls should reach it through an extension namespace, not the concrete type.

core/backends/sim/SimBackend.h.note: The synthetic demo backend (#4473) — a concrete IRadioBackend implementor that generates its own audio and spectrum, RX-only by construction (Principle VI). Reached today from ConnectionPanel.cpp, MainWindow.cpp and MainWindow_Session.cpp; pre-existing coupling, frozen into the EB3 baseline. The UI should select it through RadioModel::makeBackend()'s family string, never the concrete type.

core/tnc/Ax25Connection.h.note: Single-peer AX.25 v2.0 connected-mode (LAPB) data-link state machine, mod-8 sequence space, backing the Personal Mailbox System. Radio-agnostic packet layer above whatever modem or backend carries the audio.

models/AetherClockModel.h.note: Thin first-class AetherClock model with full Q_PROPERTY coverage (protocol-serializable, QML-ready), mirroring engine state over queued connections. Owns no DSP and has no vendor ties — one of only three models already shaped the way the protocol will want them.

models/DStarModel.h.note: D-STAR configuration and session state (callsigns, RPT1/RPT2 routing, modem/serial paths). Digital-voice state any backend carrying DV would present.

models/DigitalVoiceWaveformHistory.h.note: Rolling health history for the DV waveform path (sample rate, turnaround, deficits). Generic rate/latency telemetry fused with Flex VITA sequence-gap counters.
models/DigitalVoiceWaveformHistory.h.split: Core (universal): sample-rate validity, turnaround mean, source block deficits, RX/TX validity — health facts any DV transport has. Flex extension: vitaSequenceGapsPerSecond / txVitaSequenceGapsPerSecond, which are DAX/VITA-49 stream facts that should arrive as a backend-reported stream-health delta through the seam.

models/ModelCapabilities.h.note: Per-model capability table mirroring FlexLib ModelInfo.cs (RadioPlatform, has2Meters/has4Meters, loop A/B). This is the universal question 'what can this radio do', answered exclusively from a vendor table — and its band-availability half is precisely the band truth RFC §4.1 assigns to the capability descriptor. Consumed above the seam by SpectrumOverlayMenu, XvtrPolicy, WaveformInstallGate and MainWindow_Wiring.
models/ModelCapabilities.h.split: Core (universal): the capability question itself — tunable band set, transverter presence, extended-DSP availability — which belongs in core/backends/RadioCapabilities.h as backend-declared fields (RadioCapabilities has no band field today; adding one is the convergence step). Flex extension: the FlexLib platform taxonomy (Microburst/DeepEddy/BigBend/DragonFire) and the model-string table that derives it, which belong behind FlexBackend.

models/Nr2SettingsModel.h.note: Process-wide owner of client-side NR2 configuration as one versioned object (Principle V), so every editing surface shares state. Engine DSP configuration; radio-agnostic.

models/Rn2SettingsModel.h.note: Process-wide owner of client-side RN2 configuration as one versioned object (Principle V). Engine DSP configuration; radio-agnostic.

models/SliceLinkPolicy.h.note: Pure decision logic for Slice Link (cross-panadapter VFO link) — echo classification on integer Hz, no QObject, no I/O, no model access. Canonical slice state only.

core/DisplayPresence.h.note: Host display-presence probe used to choose the desktop Qt platform before QApplication; startup/rendering plumbing, not radio state.

core/EibiClient.h.note: Radio-agnostic EiBi shortwave schedule downloader/parser that emits canonical DX spots; engine data service with no vendor protocol coupling.

core/MiniPanSettings.h.note: Client-side persistence for the mini-pan applet span; UI configuration, not radio-owned state or a daemon protocol resource.

core/ShutdownTrace.h.note: Process-local shutdown diagnostics and support-log breadcrumbs; lifecycle plumbing, not radio state.

core/SpeProtocol.h.note: Wire codec for standalone SPE Expert amplifiers over serial/ser2net. The accessory connects independently of the radio and stays outside IRadioBackend, matching the ACOM/VKAMP peripheral precedent.

core/backends/hl2/Hl2Backend.h.note: Concrete Hermes-Lite 2 IRadioBackend implementation: HPSDR/Metis transport plus HL2-owned RX/TX DSP. Family-specific implementation belongs below the radio seam.

core/backends/hl2/Hl2FreqCal.h.note: Pure frequency-error math and radio-scoped persistence fused with the HL2 crystal/NCO model. Surface as a namespaced HL2 extension without treating generic calibration math as wire code.
core/backends/hl2/Hl2FreqCal.h.split: Core: bounded calibration math and persistence mechanics. HL2 extension: nominal clock, NCO correction semantics, zero-beat workflow and UI/automation verbs.

core/backends/icom/IcomCredentials.h.note: OS-keychain and process-session storage for an Icom network password. Credential plumbing shared by connection UI and backend, never a control-protocol field or radio-state resource.

core/backends/icom/IcomModels.h.note: Icom CI-V model identity, model-specific capability tables, and model-ID reply decoding. Family-specific knowledge belongs behind the Icom backend; the client should consume canonical capabilities.

core/backends/icom/IcomSettings.h.note: Client-side connection configuration for the Icom backend (host, username, ports and CI-V selection), with credentials explicitly excluded. Connection plumbing, not live radio state.

core/CtcssTones.h.note: Canonical CTCSS tone vocabulary shared by operator controls and automation validation. Radio-family-neutral state and validation data.

core/LpMeterProtocol.h.note: TelePost LP-100A serial protocol codec for a standalone external wattmeter. Accessory wire code outside the radio-family seam.

core/RtlSdrDiscovery.h.note: RTL-SDR USB device discovery that emits the shared RadioInfo shape. Family-specific discovery belongs below the RTL backend seam.

core/SystemInfo.h.note: Process-local per-thread CPU diagnostics and sampling math for the Runtime Monitor. Host observability plumbing, not radio state.

core/SystemInfoCollector.h.note: Worker that samples host thread CPU use for the Runtime Monitor dialog. Desktop diagnostics plumbing, not radio state.

core/SystemInventory.h.note: Startup and support-bundle inventory of host CPU, SIMD and RAM capabilities. Process diagnostics, not radio state.

core/ThreadCpuRing.h.note: Short host-thread CPU history used by Runtime Monitor peak and sparkline presentation. Diagnostic UI support, not radio state.

core/UlanziDialMacOSManager.h.note: macOS IOKit implementation of the Ulanzi Dial client input surface. Desktop hardware plumbing, not radio state.

core/backends/ConnectionSharingPolicy.h.note: Fail-closed discovery-time policy for whether a busy radio family permits another client. Canonical cross-family connection safety pending capability descriptors.

core/backends/RadioCapabilities.h.note: Backend-neutral capability descriptor consumed above the radio seam. Universal by definition; family implementations populate it.

core/backends/anan/AnanDiscovery.h.note: openHPSDR Protocol 2 discovery and ANAN-G2 identity handling. Family-specific discovery belongs below the ANAN backend seam.

core/backends/anan/AnanSettings.h.note: Client-side connection and ADC configuration for the ANAN backend. Persisted setup plumbing, not live radio state.

core/backends/anan/P2Protocol.h.note: openHPSDR Ethernet Protocol 2 wire primitives for the ANAN-G2 backend. Family protocol code belongs below the radio seam.
